findings.claim: utf8::decode($text) fails silently when the page holds any invalid UTF-8, leaving a byte string. The /u regexes then treat every byte as a Latin-1 character, so a continuation byte such as 0xA0 or 0x85 inside a valid multibyte project name (for example a trailing 'à' = C3 A0) is trimmed as white space. The later utf8::encode($project) also double-encodes any remaining high bytes. A non-ASCII project name on a page with invalid UTF-8 elsewhere is therefore reported corrupted, where the base read it byte-faithfully. The decode result is never checked, and Go's TrimSpace would not trim those bytes.

evidence: Only scripts/rehearse-card-page-migration.sh changed; the whole diff was read.
The readable-page check index($raw,"---\n",4)==$close+4 is arithmetically consistent: the closing line starts at raw offset close+4, including the empty-frontmatter case.
Perl \s under /u matches the same set as strings.TrimSpace (U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000), so valid UTF-8 pages are handled as the commit claims.
The invalid-UTF-8 path (utf8::decode returning false, then /u and utf8::encode) is the only defect found, and it is reasoned from Perl semantics, not run.
